selected.rationale: The Wellness Optimizer has category affinities for wellness and supplements and prefers science-backed claims and ingredient transparency, making her an ideal target for a functional protein bar that avoids the chalky, cardboards-like taste of typical products.

The Convenience-First Millennial defaults to what is fast and easy, with category affinities for instant delivery and quick commerce, matching the impulse-friendly, high-frequency grocery nature of protein bar purchases on platforms like Swiftcart.

The Fitness Enthusiast works out frequently and buys performance-related snacks and supplements, directly aligning with a protein bar advertiser targeting active demographics looking for better-tasting nutritional fueling.

rejected.reason: The Busy Parent prioritizes bulk buying and subscription services, whereas this advertiser operates on a one-off business model with missing subscription availability.

The Gen Z Aesthete focuses heavily on high-visual identity-expressive beauty, fashion, and small-batch decor with a playful, aesthetic-forward voice, which does not align with a functional grocery snack brand.
The Pet Parent focuses strictly on pet food, pet health, and pet supplies, which has no overlap with human protein bars and groceries.
The Affluent Classic has an older age range of 50-68 and a high AOV focused on classic apparel and home goods, which falls outside the advertiser's target age range of 18-45.

The Sustainability Buyer focuses on specific supply chain transparency and carbon footprints, whereas the advertiser's core value proposition and brief center exclusively on taste rather than environmental claims.
The Value-Conscious Shopper requires discount-forward messaging and bundle offers, which conflicts with the mid-tier, one-off $30 estimated AOV product brief.
The Gifter is explicitly disinterested in self-care-only framing and relies on gifting-holiday timelines, whereas protein bars are an everyday personal grocery snack.
